verdict_text:
NO

The merge itself is correct (float32 `B @ A`, scale 2, cast back to float16, `fan_in_fan_out` honored) and the four required checks are present. But the entire sharded export required by clause 4 ("shard files plus an index file `model.safetensors.index.json`... at most 512 MiB of tensor data per shard... single oversized tensors stored alone") is delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors` from a local `_ckpt` module that is not part of the artifact, as is the input loading via `load_checkpoint`. From reading alone there is no way to confirm that the index file is written, that the 512 MiB limit is measured on tensor bytes excluding headers, that `embed_in.weight` and `embed_out.weight` land in their own shards, or that loading preserves float16 dtypes. The condition also requires a standalone script using only PyTorch and `safetensors`, which importing a private helper module violates.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
